steps.expr: charge conjugation C acts as the degree-mirror d -> 12-d: it NEGATES the signed charge, charge(12-d) = 12-2(12-d) = -(12-2d) (29.EM.1); it is an involution (C^2 = id); and it FIXES the neutral flat site d=6 (charge 0) -- exactly the mirror that separates the right wing (d<6, +) from the left wing (d>6, -) in 36/48

steps.what: C = charge conjugation = the degree-mirror d<->12-d: it NEGATES the charge 12-2d (29), the flat mirror of the wings (36/48)
steps.why: the first discrete symmetry, and it is the wing-mirror in disguise. Charge conjugation flips the sign of every charge; the substrate's charge is the signed angle-defect 12-2d (29.EM.1). The operation that negates it is the degree-mirror d -> 12-d: charge(12-d) = 12 - 2(12-d) = 2d - 12 = -(12-2d). RUN IT: charge(5)=+2 <-> charge(7)=-2, charge(4)=+4 <-> charge(8)=-4, and d=6 (charge 0) is fixed. So C is the reflection about the FLAT MIRROR d=6 -- the very mirror that separates the min-density right wing (the twelve, 15) from the max-density left wing (the anti-twelve, 36/48). C is an involution (applying the mirror twice restores d). So charge conjugation is a built substrate operation: particle (d<6) <-> antiparticle (d>6) is right-wing <-> left-wing. (The identification C <-> the degree-mirror is a reading, CT.4; that d->12-d negates 12-2d and is an involution is the derived arithmetic.)

steps.what: P = parity = the even/odd orbit swap (44); the substrate VIOLATES P (it is chiral)
steps.why: the second discrete symmetry, already built in 44. Parity is a spatial orientation reversal; on the carrier it is the map that swaps the even-permutation orbit (the carrier) with the odd orbit (the conjugate mirror), flipping the sign +1 <-> -1 (44.CH.1). It is an involution (two reversals restore). CRUCIALLY the substrate VIOLATES P: 44.CH.2 showed the even and odd orbits are DISTINCT conjugate copies (the carrier != its mirror), so P maps the carrier off itself -- parity is not a self-symmetry. This is exactly the weak force's maximal parity violation (44.CH.3). So P is a real operation, and it is BROKEN by the substrate's chirality.

steps.expr: time reversal T reverses the ARROW of the directed succession -- the +1/-1 step direction (07.7.2) along the 1-D oriented time (46.LS.1) flips sign. It is an involution (reversing twice restores the arrow)
steps.what: T = time reversal = reversing the arrow of the directed ordinal succession (46/07); an involution
steps.why: the third discrete symmetry. Time is the 1-D oriented ordinal succession (46.LS.1), and its ARROW is the +1/-1 direction of each step (07.7.2). Time reversal T reverses that arrow: +1 <-> -1, so a forward walk becomes its backward reverse. It is an involution (T(T(x)) = x). The substrate HAS a definite arrow (07's directed succession, 46's oriented time), so T is a genuine, non-trivial operation -- the substrate is not time-symmetric at the level of the arrow (the succession has a direction), though the DYNAMICS' T-behaviour is a matter-sector question (CT.5).
